# Hyperparameters

Every tunable parameter of every imputer and method, with its type, default and bounds. This is the feature the tool exists for: in the pipeline it was ported from, all of these were unreachable, so a benchmark could never answer *would a different setting have done better?*

22 of 34 methods take parameters; the rest have nothing to tune.

## How to pass them

```bash
# one method, one parameter
combobatch run --exp e.tsv.gz --ann a.csv --out out/ \
    --batch-col BATCH --bio-col CLASS \
    --imputation knn --method 10_mnn --method-params '10_mnn:k=50'

# several, and on the imputer too
combobatch dispatch --config base.yaml \
    --method-params '10_mnn:k=50,11_harmony:n_pcs=30' \
    --imputation-params 'knn:knn_k=15'
```

```yaml
methods:
  - name: 10_mnn            # defaults
  - name: 10_mnn            # and a second run at k = 50
    params: {k: 50}
```

A parameter name that no method declares is rejected **before** anything is downloaded, with a did-you-mean suggestion. So is a value of the wrong type.

## What tuning does to the output name

A selection that is not at pure defaults gets a parameter tag, so two runs of one method cannot overwrite each other:

```
strict__10_mnn.tsv.gz          # defaults - no tag
strict__10_mnn__k50.tsv.gz     # k = 50
```

`run_manifest.json` maps every tag back to the parameters it stands for. The imputer and the method share one tag slot, so tuning the same parameter name on both sides is rejected rather than silently resolved. Override a generated tag with `param_tag` when it would otherwise be unwieldy.

## Imputers

### `strict`

No imputation: every gene with a missing value is dropped. The max_na_frac = 0.0 corner of one uniform rule, not a separate code path.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Bounds | Meaning | R argument |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_na_frac` | float | `0.0` | min 0.0, max 0.0 | Fixed at 0.0 for strict: a gene with any NA is dropped. | — |

### `knn`

k-nearest-neighbour imputation (scikit-learn).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Bounds | Meaning | R argument |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_na_frac` | float | `0.2` | min 0.0, max 1.0 | Drop genes whose NA fraction exceeds this before imputing. 0.0 means drop any gene with a single missing value, which is what 'strict' does. | — |
| `knn_k` | int | `5` | min 1 | Neighbours used per missing value. | — |
| `weights` | str | `'uniform'` | one of `uniform`, `distance` | Neighbour weighting. | — |
| `metric` | str | `'nan_euclidean'` | one of `nan_euclidean` | Distance metric tolerant of missing values. | — |

### `softimpute`

Soft-thresholded SVD matrix completion (R softImpute).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Bounds | Meaning | R argument |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_na_frac` | float | `0.2` | min 0.0, max 1.0 | Drop genes whose NA fraction exceeds this before imputing. 0.0 means drop any gene with a single missing value, which is what 'strict' does. | — |
| `rank_max` | int | `None` | min 1 | Maximum solution rank. | `softImpute(rank.max=)` |
| `lambda_` | float | `None` | min 0.0 | Nuclear-norm penalty. | `softImpute(lambda=)` |
| `thresh` | float | `None` | min 0.0 | Convergence threshold. | `softImpute(thresh=)` |
| `maxit` | int | `None` | min 1 | Maximum iterations. | `softImpute(maxit=)` |
| `type` | str | `'svd'` | one of `svd`, `als` | Algorithm variant. | `softImpute(type=)` |

### `missforest`

Random-forest iterative imputation (R missForest).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Bounds | Meaning | R argument |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_na_frac` | float | `0.2` | min 0.0, max 1.0 | Drop genes whose NA fraction exceeds this before imputing. 0.0 means drop any gene with a single missing value, which is what 'strict' does. | — |
| `ntree` | int | `None` | min 1 | Trees per forest. | `missForest(ntree=)` |
| `maxiter` | int | `None` | min 1 | Maximum imputation iterations. | `missForest(maxiter=)` |
| `mtry` | int | `None` | min 1 | Variables sampled per split. | `missForest(mtry=)` |

### `20_shambhala`

Borisov et al. 2021, Bioinformatics (Shambhala2); CuBlock.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Bounds | Meaning | R argument |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `P` | str | `None` | — | Calibration reference P, the quantile-normalization anchor. Path or s3:// URI; defaults to the shipped P0_standard. | — |
| `Q` | str | `None` | — | Calibration reference Q, whose per-gene log mean and std define the target shape. Path or s3:// URI; defaults to the shipped Q0_standard. | — |
| `k` | int | `5` | min 2 | k-means gene clusters for CuBlock. | — |
| `n_workers` | int | `1` | min 1, max 10 | Shambhala worker processes. Defaults to 1: this multiplies with the dispatcher's own workers to give the total Octave process count. | — |
| `na_strategy` | str | `'drop'` | one of `drop`, `knn` | NaN handling before Octave, which cannot accept missing values. 'drop' restores affected genes as NaN afterwards; 'knn' imputes them. | — |
| `knn_k` | int | `5` | min 1 | Neighbours for na_strategy='knn'. | — |
| `max_na_frac` | float | `0.2` | min 0.0, max 1.0 | Genes above this NaN fraction are dropped rather than imputed, for na_strategy='knn'. | — |
| `q_pseudocount` | float | `1e-06` | min 0.0 | Added to Q before the log so zero counts do not become -Inf. 0 excludes zero-count genes instead. | — |
| `random_seed` | int | `None` | — | Seeds Octave's k-means for reproducible CuBlock output. | — |
| `octave_bin` | str | `'octave'` | — | Octave executable. The image places it on PATH. | — |
| `timeout_s` | int | `6000` | min 1 | Per-batch Octave subprocess timeout, in seconds. | — |
| `precompute_qn_reference` | bool | `False` | — | Quantile-normalize Python-side against a reference distribution taken from P and skip Octave's own pass. Large speed-up, near-lossless. | — |
| `synthetic_cublock_p` | bool | `False` | — | Give CuBlock one synthetic P column instead of all P samples. | — |
| `max_p_samples` | int | `None` | min 1 | Subsample P to its N centroid-closest samples. | — |
| `precompute_cublock_clusters` | bool | `False` | — | Cluster genes once from P and reuse the assignment for every sample, instead of 30 k-means runs per sample. | — |
| `python_cublock` | bool | `False` | — | Experimental pure-Python CuBlock. Upstream measures ~226% mean relative difference against Octave; not equivalent. | — |

## Methods with nothing to tune

`01_raw`, `02_median_scaling`, `07_pycombat`, `08_inmoose_combatseq`, `17_quantile`, `18_rank`, `30_recombat`, `03_limma`, `04_sva`, `05_combat`, `06_combat_seq`, `14_qsmooth`

## Which parameters actually matter

From the source benchmark's variance decomposition, the choice of **method** dominates (36.3% of outcome variance), then the **subset** of data (25.6%), then **imputation** (1.6%), then post-removal (0.2%). Tuning within a method moves results far less than choosing a different method — so sweep across methods first, and tune second.

Two exceptions worth the time: `10_mnn`'s `k`, which controls how aggressively batches are merged and interacts strongly with batch size, and `target_group` on the reference-based methods, which decides *which* platform everything else is mapped onto.
